analysis:
Both units are head_text excerpts of CHANGELOG.md, lines 2571-2979. They are historical release notes for v0.9.10 through v0.9.17 and the tail of an unpublished v0.10.6 candidate section. The patch shows the file grows from about 9 lines to about 804 changed head lines. The excerpt contains documentation only. No executable code, configuration, workflow, permission or secret handling is changed. I checked it against the threat model.

Security-relevant claims in the text, such as SEC-035 re-acceptance and the 30-minute SSD cache TTL (T-041), were already recorded in the base threat model. The App Attest statements stay consistent with TB-011/T-052 through T-057: diagnostics are outside the signed transcript and do not affect authorization. The unauthenticated earnings endpoint removal (T-031) is a mitigation, not a regression. I found no sign that these notes alter or contradict the documented trust boundaries.

Remaining uncertainty is outside these units. The v0.10.6 candidate section (lines 11-808) describes two-Mac cluster serving, RDMA over Thunderbolt, `cluster_runtime` registration fields, and cluster approvals and grants derived from releases. That would be new attack surface at the coordinator-to-provider boundary and for the provider cluster trust model. It is not visible in the supplied excerpts and is not described in the canonical threat model. The corresponding code changes were not supplied in this batch. The next review pass should check whether the threat model needs a new boundary for inter-Mac RDMA/cluster peer trust and for the `cluster_runtime` attestation-adjacent fields. A changelog is not evidence that any behavior is implemented or safe.
